output.whyThisAltersJudgment: The position depended on regulated buyers being able to move beyond pilots. For one regulated segment, US government, the new evidence removes two stated frictions: price (a 40% discount across every product surface and every level of government) and commitment (no minimum spend), through an existing GSA schedule, with a FedRAMP High offering that includes coding and agentic capabilities now generally available. That raises confidence in the public-sector part of the thesis. It does not satisfy V1: GSA provides a vehicle for others, and no individual organisation has publicly committed to organisation-wide coding-agent use. The usage figures are self-reported, and the source's legacy-code anecdotes failed verification, so the 'legacy modernisation as entry point' part is not strengthened. The IPO claims do not bear on the position.
output.publicLine: New vendor-reported evidence from US government — a 40% discount across every level of government with no minimum spend, and a FedRAMP High offering with coding capabilities now generally available — strengthens the public-sector part of this thesis. It does not meet the validation condition: no individual organisation has yet committed to organisation-wide coding-agent use, and the figures are self-reported.
